title: Org-user write endpoints redirect to k8s only for current-org + single-org + flag
answers: Why doesn't deleting an org user use the kubernetes User API?
How do I add a new org-user write path to the kubernetesUsersRedirect migration?
Why does DELETE /api/org/users/:userId behave differently from /api/orgs/:orgId/users/:userId?
body:
Symptom: org write operations (update/remove) sometimes act on stale data because legacy org_user table can be empty/out of sync once reads are served from k8s User search.
Root cause: write paths kept calling the legacy org service even after reads moved to k8s (pkg/api/org_users.go:removeOrgUserHelper before this PR).
Fix pattern: in the handler, redirect to a *UsingK8s variant only when cmd.OrgID == c.GetOrgID() (i.e. the 'current org' endpoint, not the cross-org admin endpoint) AND hs.Cfg.RBAC.SingleOrganization AND the FlagKubernetesUsersRedirect openfeature flag is true; otherwise fall through to the existing orgService call unchanged.
Constraints: only applies to single-org deployments; the cross-org variant (RemoveOrgUser/admin org users) intentionally keeps the legacy path and is unaffected — do not extend the redirect to it without separate review.
applies: pkg/api/org_users.go write handlers (update/remove org user) gated by FlagKubernetesUsersRedirect
says: Organization user deletion still uses old data instead of kubernetes backend
Why don't org user delete requests use the kubernetes user API

Organization user updates not synced to kubernetes database

search: Org-user write handlers in pkg/api/org_users.go (removeOrgUserHelper, update operations) redirect to *UsingK8s variants only when three conditions are met: cmd.OrgID == c.GetOrgID() (current-org endpoint only, not cross-org admin), hs.Cfg.RBAC.SingleOrganization is true, and FlagKubernetesUsersRedirect feature flag is enabled. Otherwise fall through to the legacy orgService path unchanged. Single-org deployments avoid stale data from the legacy org_user table; the cross-org RemoveOrgUser endpoint intentionally remains on the legacy path.
